# Applying the patches

<!-- Generated by `node src/report.js` from results/apply/*.json. Do not edit. -->

Of the 246 vectors, 208 are patches in the plain sense: the vector records the file tree before and the file tree after, and the diff is what git or GNU diff printed for the two. For each of them the old tree is written to an empty directory, the program under test applies the diff there, and the directory is read back and compared with the new tree, byte for byte, file modes and symbolic links included. A library that patches one file at a time is given each file section together with the old content of that file.

There are four ways this can end:

| | the program said | and the files are |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **right** | done | exactly the new tree |
| **refused** | error | untouched |
| **left half-done** | error | changed, and not the new tree |
| **wrong** | done | not the new tree |

**Read this first.**

- "Refused" is a limitation: the caller is told, and nothing is lost. "Wrong" is the column that matters — a file with different content, a file that should be gone, a file that is gone and should not be, and no error to say so.
- This is not a ranking. The corpus collects hard cases; every one of these programs applies an ordinary patch correctly.
- Every diff here is unmodified output of git or GNU diff, applied to exactly the tree it was made from. Nothing is fuzzy, offset or already applied.
- The invocation is in the table. Other options give other results; `git apply --unidiff-zero` is listed next to `git apply` to show one such case.
- The versions are the ones installed where this was run. What was already known to each project is in [`FINDINGS.md`](FINDINGS.md).

The reference appliers are part of this repository (`src/refapply.js`, `reference/python/udiff_reference.py`). They are in the table to show that every one of these patches can be applied from its text and the old files alone. A library that patches one file at a time is not given the vectors in which no file content changes (pure renames, mode changes), and a library that takes text is not given files that are not valid UTF-8; that is why the number of patches differs.

### gnu-patch

GNU patch 2.7.6 · C · <https://savannah.gnu.org/projects/patch/>

- Under test: `patch -pN -f --no-backup-if-mismatch -i FILE` — on a directory
- -f: never ask. --no-backup-if-mismatch: no .orig files next to a file patched with fuzz or at an offset, so that only what patch did to the files themselves is compared. Rejects (.rej) are left where patch puts them.

195 of 208 patches are applied correctly.

### bsd-patch

BSD patch 2.0-12u11 FreeBSD · C · <https://cgit.freebsd.org/src/tree/usr.bin/patch>

- Under test: `patch -pN -f -s -E -V none -i FILE` — on a directory
- -f: never ask. -s: print only what went wrong. -E: remove a file that is empty after patching; without it a file the patch deletes is left as an empty file, and the ports framework of FreeBSD passes it too (Mk/bsd.port.mk, PATCH_ARGS). -V none: no FILE.orig next to every patched file (made unless --posix is given), so that only what patch did to the files themselves is compared. Rejects (.rej) are left where patch puts them.

140 of 208 patches are applied correctly.

- The old text is cut into lines the way the reader cuts the patch (BufferedReader.readLine), and the lines that come back are joined with LF.

176 of 184 patches are applied correctly.

**Wrong without an error (4):**

| vector | what is in the directory afterwards |
| --- | --- |
| `git/bytes/crlf-file-modified` | "win.txt": 13 bytes, expected 16; first difference at byte 3 (line 1): expected "one\r\nTWO\r\nthree\r", got "one\nTWO\nthree" |
| `git/bytes/lf-to-crlf` | "conv.txt": 7 bytes, expected 9; first difference at byte 3 (line 1): expected "one\r\ntwo\r", got "one\ntwo" |
| `git/bytes/mixed-line-endings` | "mixed.txt": 7 bytes, expected 9; first difference at byte 3 (line 2): expected "a\nb\r\nc\r\nD", got "a\nb\nc\nD" |
| `gnu/crlf` | "w.txt": 7 bytes, expected 9; first difference at byte 3 (line 1): expected "one\r\nTWO\r", got "one\nTWO" |

**Refused (4):**

| what it said | vectors | for example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UnifiedDiffParserException: expected data line not found | 3 | `git/content/section-heading-with-control-characters` |
| UnifiedDiffParserException: expected file start line not found | 1 | `git/ops/rewrite-with-dissimilarity` |

## Reproducing

```
node src/apply.js                         # every applier; writes results/apply/*.json
node src/apply.js --adapter gnu-patch --show
node src/report.js                        # this file
```
